evals.name: full-run-static-site-fixture
evals.prompt: Copy evals/fixtures/tidepool to a scratch folder and make it professional and navigable top to bottom: layout, READMEs, the docs tree, a roadmap and a changelog. It's a plain static page with no build step. The GitHub repo is example-org/tidepool and it isn't live anywhere yet.
evals.expected_output: Layout (§1.1): index.html, styles.css and app.js move off the root into site/ (static, no build, so site/ not src/), and the move keeps index.html's relative styles.css/app.js references working; docs/guides/install.md is updated to say open site/index.html. Root README: no logo asset exists, so it falls back to a plain H1 title (or asks for a logo path) and never invents an image path; no Live Demo badge or demo link, since there is no live URL, and no leftover ⟨…⟩ placeholder; a 'what's in here' table with bold leftmost-column links down to site/README.md and docs/README.md. Every non-root README (site/, docs/, docs/architecture/) opens with the §3.2 header: centered emoji <h1> with the emoji on the left, one-sentence italic tagline, 1-3 for-the-badge badges, a --- divider; none gets the logo hero, none stays a bare # heading. docs/README.md links to architecture/README.md, NOT straight to architecture/overview.md; a new docs/architecture/README.md (Tier 3) links down to overview.md and data-model.md. docs/guides/ holds one document, so it gets NO README of its own and install.md is linked directly from the hub (§2.4). Every index has a centered footer nav row with an up-link to its parent. docs/ROADMAP.md follows references/roadmap-standard.md: centered header, '## <emoji> Phase N: <name>' headings, every item a '- [ ]' line, items include the TODO (station picker) and FIXME (blank chart on an API error) from app.js written as checkable sentences, plus non-code work (go live at a URL, licence, promotion); a '## 🚦' go-live phase immediately before exactly one '## After public release' or '## After go-live' heading, with 'Nothing below blocks go-live.' under it; no invented dates. docs/CHANGELOG.md exists beside it under a plain date heading (the fixture has no tags or history of its own, so no invented version numbers like 1.0.0; the enclosing agent-skills git log is not this project's history) and records this restructure. The hub links both files. Voice: the existing slop is gone (serves as, comprehensive, seamless, showcasing, robust, empowering, 'not just X, it's Y', Blazing-fast, 'Happy coding!', the curly apostrophe, the restating '**Charts:** Charts are displayed' bullet); the §5 step-9 grep finds no live hits in prose. No diagram is added.

evals.name: header-only-root-hero
evals.prompt: Only replace the header at the top of my repo-root README, leave the rest alone. Project: Harbor Watch, a dashboard that shows live berth occupancy for small marinas. Live at https://harbor-watch.dev, repo github.com/example-org/harbor-watch, docs in docs/README.md, logo at images/logo/harbor-watch-landscape.svg. Stack: TypeScript 5.6, React 19, Vite 6, PostgreSQL 17. It's an early prototype. The current file starts with '# Harbor Watch' followed by a '## Features' section.
evals.expected_output:
Only the top block changes: the '# Harbor Watch' line is replaced and everything from '## Features' down is byte-identical. The new block is the §3.1 root hero with exactly these eight elements in order, each in its own

where applicable: ; the logo images/logo/harbor-watch-landscape.svg linked to https://harbor-watch.dev with width="720" and an alt that is a full sentence saying what the project is (not just 'Harbor Watch'); an italic tagline split across two lines with
that says what the dashboard does; a bold 'Explore the docs »' link to docs/README.md; a nav row of three links joined by middle dots (a demo link, Report Bug and Request Feature both pointing at the repo's issues URL); three for-the-badge hero badges: a green 2ea44f Live Demo badge with logo=vercel whose host value escapes the dash as harbor--watch.dev, a status badge in amber F59E0B (experimental or MVP_Prototype), and a purple 8B5CF6 roadmap badge linking docs/ROADMAP.md; four flat-square tech badges (TypeScript 3178C6, React 61DAFB, Vite, PostgreSQL 4169E1) with brand logo slugs, never mixed into the hero row; then a single ---. No ⟨…⟩ placeholders, no '|' or comma inside a badge value, straight quotes only, and the tagline avoids the §0 tells (comprehensive, seamless, robust, powerful, -ing tails).

evals.name: roadmap-only-whats-left
evals.prompt: What's left before I can launch this? Write it down as the roadmap and don't touch anything else. It's a Next.js app for booking dog-grooming appointments, going public. Done so far: booking flow, Postgres schema, auth with magic links. Not done: Stripe deposits, SMS reminders, no domain bought, no landing page copy, no tests in CI, no licence, nobody knows it exists, and I haven't decided pricing.
evals.expected_output: Writes docs/ROADMAP.md (not the repo root, not a sub-folder) and changes no other file, except optionally adding a ROADMAP row to an existing docs/README.md catalog. The file matches references/roadmap-standard.md: centered '🗺️ Roadmap' header with an italic one-line tagline and badges (amber 'now', green 'stage', gray '↩ docs_home' back to README.md); the intro paragraph saying every item above the go-live heading is a gate; the marker legend; phases as '## <emoji> Phase N: <name>' in blocking order; every work item a '- [ ]' (or '- [x]' for the three finished things, which may carry no invented done date) line that someone else could mark done, e.g. 'Stripe deposit charged at booking in test mode, refund on cancel' rather than 'Payments'; the '## 🚦 Public release' phase holds CI green with tests, README verified from a clean clone, SECURITY.md plus a clean secret scan, the licence, and live at its URL; then exactly one '## After public release' heading with 'Nothing below blocks go-live.' and ### groups for Publish and promote (domain, landing copy, launch post) and Revenue (pricing). Owner-only decisions (licence, pricing) end in '🔒 Needs owner'. Non-code work is present, not just features. No target dates are invented. A centered footer links back to README.md and on to CHANGELOG.md. Prose passes §0.

evals.name: tick-roadmap-item-and-log-it
evals.prompt: Stripe checkout is live in test mode now (one plan, receipt email works). Tick it off the roadmap and bring the changelog up to date. The roadmap line in docs/ROADMAP.md under '### 💰 Revenue' is '- [ ] Stripe checkout live in test mode, one plan, receipt email sends'. docs/CHANGELOG.md is unversioned and its newest heading is '## 2026-10-30'. The README's Pricing section still says 'Payments are coming soon.'
evals.expected_output: The roadmap line becomes '- [x] Stripe checkout live in test mode, one plan, receipt email sends — done YYYY-MM-DD: <what landed, where>' using the real current date taken from the environment; the item is kept, not deleted. docs/CHANGELOG.md gets a NEW date heading for today placed above '## 2026-10-30' (newest first), with the entry under '**Added**', written as one past-tense sentence about what changed for a user of the project (not 'Refactored checkout handler') and tagged '*(roadmap: Revenue)*' in italics. No version number is invented for this unversioned project. The stale README line 'Payments are coming soon.' is updated in the same change, because a tick also updates any doc it made stale. If the agent commits, all three files go in one commit.

evals.name: humanize-only-keep-house-style
evals.prompt:
The structure of this docs/README.md is fine but the writing sounds like ChatGPT. Fix the prose only.

📚 Documentation

A comprehensive hub that serves as the central gateway to the platform's robust, end-to-end capabilities.

--- ## 🚀 Guides | Guide | Purpose | |:---|:---| | [**⚙️ Setup**](setup/README.md) | Setup instructions for setting up the project seamlessly. | | [**🔌 API**](api/README.md) | Delves into the intricate API landscape, showcasing every endpoint and ensuring developers can leverage its full power. | Additionally, it is important to note that these docs are constantly evolving — reflecting the team's commitment to excellence — and the future looks bright!
evals.expected_output: Returns the same file with the structure untouched: the centered emoji <h1>, the badge and its link, the --- divider, the '## 🚀 Guides' emoji heading, and the bold leftmost-column links stay exactly as they were (§0.1: removing them is the over-correction anti-pattern). Only prose changes: the tagline says what is in the folder instead of what it represents, with no 'comprehensive', 'serves as', 'robust' or 'gateway'; the Setup cell no longer restates the row name and drops 'seamlessly'; the API cell drops delves/intricate/landscape/showcasing/ensuring/leverage and says something concrete or stays short; the closing paragraph (Additionally, 'it is important to note', 'constantly evolving', the -ing tail, 'the future looks bright') is cut or reduced to a real fact. 'end-to-end' may keep its hyphen if the phrase survives. No more than one em dash per paragraph, straight quotes only. The rewrite does not invent facts the original never stated (no made-up endpoint counts or setup times). The §5 step-9 grep finds no remaining hits in prose.

evals.name: obsidian-vault-no-roadmap
evals.prompt: My Obsidian vault of personal recipes is a mess, folders by cuisine with no index notes and nothing links anywhere. Make it navigable from the top, and give it the usual roadmap and changelog too. It's just for me, I'm never publishing it.
evals.expected_output: Applies §2 and §7 for a doc library: the top-level cuisine folders are the content categories, each gets a README.md index (§3.2 folder header, bold leftmost-column catalog of its immediate children, a footer up-link), the root README links down to each cuisine folder, a folder with a single note gets no README of its own and that note is linked from the parent, and every link is relative with no markdown nested inside the HTML header tags so it renders in Obsidian. It skips §1.1 entirely (no src/ or site/ move). It does NOT write a ROADMAP.md: a personal vault with nothing to ship skips the roadmap (§2.5, §7), and the agent says so in one line instead of silently obeying or silently skipping. The changelog is optional here (§2.5: only if the collection changes often enough to be worth tracking); the agent either skips it with a one-line reason or asks, rather than writing one by reflex. No go-live, promotion or revenue items appear anywhere.
